target: PATO colorless (PATO_0000337) under PATO color (PATO_0000014), or treat 'colorless' as a colour value alongside FLOPO white
reason: White and colorless are alternative colour states of pulp. A missing subclass link of colorless under color is the gap, so a secondary union is not needed.

'Straw-colored or maroon' is grounded wrongly: maroon is a dark red-purple and not 'red', and straw yellow is a hue. Both are colours, so this is a 07a case once the colour values are grounded correctly.

Capitate (head-like, e.g. of a stigma) and subglobose are both shapes of the same part. They belong to 07a under shape, and 'subglobose' is wrongly grounded to spheroid. Fix the grounding rather than accept a cross-attribute union.
Erect (orientation or posture) or falcate (curvature) are real alternatives of the habit of leaves. Both groundings fit.
'Equal or oblique' refers to leaf base or lobe symmetry. 'Oblique' there is an asymmetry and not an orientation, so PATO oblique orientation is a wrong grounding.

target: Surface texture: place FLOPO mammillate under a PATO surface-texture parent such as PATO_0000701 smooth's attribute (surface texture)
reason: Mammillose or smooth are alternative surface textures. Both should share the surface-texture attribute, so the FLOPO class needs a parent link.

target: PATO color (PATO_0000014): straw yellow (PATO_0104343) should be a subclass of yellow or color
reason: Straw-colored or pale green are both colours. The straw yellow class lacks a link to the colour hierarchy shared with the FLOPO colour classes.

target: Common parent 'stigma shape' (or shape) for FLOPO capitate and FLOPO peltate
reason: Stigma peltate or capitate are alternative shapes of one part. Both are FLOPO value classes, so they need a shared shape parent.
Straight (form) or secund when dry (one-sided arrangement) are real alternatives of the orientation or arrangement of parts. The condition 'when dry' does not change the pair.

target: Common parent 'position relative to a surrounding part' (included vs. exserted/protruding)
reason: Included or protruding are opposite ends of the same character. They need a shared parent for exsertion.
The first value is a wrong grounding: 'greenish-cinereous' is not blue. Canescent is an indumentum or colour of hairs, so the pair mixes characters.
'Parallelodromous' is a venation class and not 'parallel'. Convergent or parallel describes orientation of parts, so the grounding of parallel is wrong.
Barbed or ciliate margins are real alternatives of margin ornamentation. Both groundings fit.
Ascending (orientation) or lax (looseness, density) are plausible alternatives for the habit of an inflorescence or branches. 'Loose' has the right sense for lax.

target: Common parent 'orientation' or 'pendency' for FLOPO descending (declined) and PATO drooping
reason: Declined or nodding are the same character: a downward-bending pedicel. They need a shared attribute.

target: Common parent 'inflorescence shape' for FLOPO umbelliform and cyme-like
reason: Umbelliform or cymiform arrays are alternatives of one character, arrangement of the inflorescence. Both are FLOPO classes without a shared parent.

target: Common parent 'resemblance to another organ' (petaloid, sepaloid) in FLOPO
reason: Petaloid or sepaloid are two values of one character, resemblance to an organ. They should share a parent.

target: PATO color (PATO_0000014): straw yellow (PATO_0104343) should be under yellow or color
reason: Straw-colored or purplish are both colours. Straw yellow lacks a link to the colour hierarchy.
Spreading (orientation) or subfalcate (curvature) are real alternatives of the habit of leaves. Both groundings fit.

target: Common parent 'orientation' or 'posture' for FLOPO inflexed and PATO erect
reason: Inflexed or erect are alternative orientations of one character. They should share an attribute.
'Callose' here means thickened (callous), a different character from flat shape. The grounding of callose is doubtful, and the example also gives 'below apex', which is a different location.
Emergent or exserted are close synonyms of position relative to an enclosing part. They need a shared parent.
Black or mottled are real alternatives of the colour or colour pattern of a part. Both groundings fit.

target: Common parent 'orientation' or 'posture' for curved (arcuate) and pendent
reason: Arcuate or pendent are alternative postures of an inflorescence. They are close in meaning and should share an attribute.
The example is 'erect-patent or erose'. Erose is a margin form and ascending is a wrong grounding of 'erect-patent', so the pair mixes characters.

target: PATO surface texture: wrinkled and ridged under a common sculpture or surface-texture parent
reason: Ridged or wrinkled are alternative surface sculptures. They should share a parent.

target: Surface or apex ornamentation parent for FLOPO coronate and PATO smooth
reason: Smooth or coronate are alternative states of apex ornamentation. They need a shared attribute.

target: Common parent 'orientation' for suberect (PATO_0002260) and reflexed or deflexed (PATO_0104353)
reason: Suberect or deflexed are alternative orientations of the blade. They need a shared parent. Deflexed is also not the same as reflexed.
The example is a single word, 'mammiform', with no 'or'. The pair comes from a split of one term into two groundings.
Erect or somewhat expanding are real alternatives of the posture of leaves in a moss. The grounding of expanding as dilated is acceptable.
The example is just 'opposite', with no 'or'. The pair comes from a split of one term into two groundings, and pseudoverticillate is wrong.

target: Common parent 'orientation' for squarrose and recurved in FLOPO
reason: Squarrose or squarrose-recurved are variants of one character, the spreading or recurving of leaves. They need a shared attribute.
The example 'shallowly rugose' has no 'or'. One word was given two groundings, rugose and foveate.
Erect (posture) or revolute (margin rolling) are real alternatives for the state of a blade. They are two different attributes, so a secondary union is appropriate.
Lobed or interrupted are real alternatives for the form of a part, e.g. an inflorescence. Both groundings fit. 'In the lower part' applies to both.

target: Common parent 'orientation' or 'arrangement' for imbricate and erect
reason: Appressed-imbricate or erect are alternative states of leaf posture when moist or dry. They need a shared attribute.
'Septate or porose' pairs a septum character with a pore character. Split is a wrong grounding of 'septate' and the two are not alternatives of one trait.
The example 'anticous pair either included' gives no alternative. Conspicuous is a visibility character and not a position, so it is a wrong grounding.
Expanded or rolled are real alternatives of the state of a margin or blade. Both groundings fit.

target: Common parent 'apex shape' or 'shape' for caudate and filiform
reason: Linear-caudate or filiform are alternative shapes of one part. They should share a shape attribute.
